newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hong Kong's CM Telecom launches IPO in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's CM Telecom launches IPO in Singapore.

text.p: Hong Kong-based CM Telecom International Ltd launched an initial public share offer (IPO) in Singapore on Monday to raise capital for expansion into the tiny but rapidly growing Chinese telecommunications market.

CM Telecom chairman Tony Hau said the IPO of 75.98 million shares at US$0.32 per share will generate net proceeds of US$17.5 million to be invested in one of China's first nationwide paging networks and also in radio communication systems in the country.

"The China market is still growing rapidly and we are cooperating with the Chinese government operators to grow with it," Hau told Reuters in an interview shortly after announcing the terms of the IPO.

CM Telecom is the first company to list on the Foreign Board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES). The board was created this year for overseas firms with a good but short track record or for companies in businesses which are thought to carry a higher than normal risk.
To conform with the SES's terms for a Foreign Board listing, which require shares to be traded in large units, CM Telecom's shares are offered in lots of 7,000 shares at US$2,240 each.
Of the total 10,855 board lots, which represent 22 percent of CM Telecom's enlarged issue capital, 2,171 are offered to the public with the remaining 8,684 placed out privately.

Founded by Hau in 1990, CM Telecom has ballooned from a small Hong Kong telecoms equipment trader to a diversified company selling and licensing mobile telephone and pager services across southern China with 20 units and associates.
In the year to March 31, 1996, the company made a net profit of HK$81 million (US$10.48 million) on a turnover of HK$619 million, Hau said.
Of this turnover, HK$440 million came from the firm's trading operations, selling Motorola, NEC, Panasonic and Casio pagers and mobile phones.
But Hau said the firm's big growth area, which the proceeds from the IPO will fund, is in its new paging networks in China.
The firm is investing in three telecoms projects in China, all of them in close cooperation with state authorities.

The biggest is a HK$165 million nationwide China paging network being developed by Shenzhen Motion Telecom Service Co Ltd, a joint venture with China Motion Telecom Development Co (CMTD), a company controlled by the Shenzhen municipal government.
CM Telecom is collaborating with CMTD to establish a microwave radio system in China designed to increase the speed and quality of its paging network.
CM Telecom and CMTD are also working with China's Guangdong Province to build a trunk radio system to monitor the movement of vehicles and goods between Hong Kong and China.
Hau said the Chinese pager market had enormous potential because pagers had so far penetrated only 1.6 percent of their potential market in the country.
"China is the most important market," he said. "There are many opportunities for foreign investors (if they)...tie up with some state-owned partners. That is the way we are investing."

A spokeswoman for brokerage Vickers Ballas, the IPO managers, said the IPO shares were being offered at a historical price-earnings ratio of 7.3 times, based on net earnings of 4.4 cents per share for the financial year ended March 31, 1996.
CM Telecom's share offer will close on October 15.
